subject: Sustained response-time outliers from Finovia - request for investigation
messages:
From: Elena Khan <elena.khan@finovia.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finovia-support.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe delays and increased error rate on inference calls - urgent

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a new class of slow responses since last night: a small percentage (~0.6%) of requests jump from our usual ~120ms median to 6-12s, and error rates have crept from 0.1% to ~1.8% over the last 8 hours. This is impacting our ingestion pipeline and downstream model scoring.

We've collected a set of traces and a small sample payloads (attached). The slow requests show long queue-wait times before they hit the model and occasional 5xxs immediately after the long wait. Can you confirm whether Redwood is running a scheduled deployment or maintenance that might have changed autoscaling/concurrency behavior?

We need an initial triage and ETA for mitigation — our SREs are standing by and can provide additional logs.

Thanks,
Elena Khan
Head of Platform Reliability
Finovia Analytics

Attachments: finovia_p99_sample_traces.zip, customer-error-log-20260719.txt

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Khan <elena.khan@finovia.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe delays and increased error rate on inference calls - urgent

Hi Elena — thanks for the samples, and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating immediately.

Neha / Sean: assigning to you for initial triage. Key asks:
- Confirm whether the traces correspond to periods of visible queueing/backpressure on the gateway (and whether the concurrency cap or token-bucket limits are being hit).
- Check whether any rolling rollout, model swap, or kernel change occurred in the last 24h for Finovia's model variant.
- If we can reproduce, try a short canary rollback to the prior model variant/config and measure p99.

Elena: we'll update you within 60 minutes with next steps.

— Grace
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 08:12 Elena Khan <elena.khan@finovia.com> wrote:
> > We're seeing a new class of slow responses since last night...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe delays and increased error rate on inference calls - urgent

Quick update from infra: we've correlated the customer's timestamps to a pattern of request spikes that produce long prefix queue times on one of our edge pools in us-west-2. Observations:

- The edge pool experienced brief saturation events between 02:30-04:10 UTC (customer timestamps). Bulk of requests completed quickly, but ~0.5-0.9% observed with queue wait > 3s before dispatch.
- Concurrent connections to the model-op pods are being capped by a conservative concurrency limit applied to that tenant's Dedicated instance (configured last quarter to reduce noisy-neighbor risk). That cap appears to be the bottleneck when request bursts exceed average concurrency.
- There is evidence of our backpressure heuristics delaying dispatch for certain long-context requests (KV cache misses). Those requests are also heavier CPU-wise on the runtime.

Next actions I kicked off:
1) Temporarily raise the per-tenant concurrency cap by 2x for Finovia (seats permitting) and monitor p99/5xx for 10 minutes.
2) Disable the conservative backpressure delay for the specific model variant to see if latency tail improves.
3) Collect flamegraphs / CPU utilization for the runtime during a reproduced burst.

Marcus: can you prepare a quick rollback plan if the raised cap causes resource contention for other tenants?

Will report back with the 10-minute window metrics.

— Neha
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe delays and increased error rate on inference calls - urgent

Good call. If we bump the cap we need a conservative rollback guardrail. Plan:
- Increase concurrency cap for Finovia by 2x on the affected pool.
- Add a short-term auto-fallback rule: if aggregate CPU% on the pool exceeds 78% for 30s or error rate > 2.5% for 2m, automatically revert cap to previous value and route excess requests to our spare burst nodes.
- Notify platform team and increase sampling rate of tracing for the tenant to 100% for 20 minutes.

I'll stand by to trigger rollback if we see negative impact. Neha: please post the 10-minute p99/5xx numbers to this thread.

— Marcus
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Khan <elena.khan@finovia.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe delays and increased error rate on inference calls - urgent

Update for Finovia / ops:

We temporarily increased the concurrency cap and disabled the backpressure delay for the model variant at 09:25 PT. Immediate results (10-minute window):
- p50 unchanged ~115ms; p95 from 420ms -> 310ms; p99 dropped from ~9.2s to ~1.1s.
- 5xxs dropped from ~1.8% to 0.4% in the window sampled.
- CPU on the affected pool rose from 52% -> 64% (within guardrail). No cross-tenant throttles observed.

We have the temporary rule active to auto-revert if CPU >78% for 30s or errors spike. Traces attached in the earlier packet show the queue wait prior to dispatch; after the change traces show much shorter queue times.

Next steps:
- We'll keep the raised cap for the next 6 hours while we run a targeted optimization: reduce KV-cache miss penalty by adjusting cache windowing and prefetch heuristics for long-context requests.
- Our perf team will produce a short write-up with recommended long-term config changes (quantization/kernel selection trade-offs) by EOD.

Elena — can we schedule a 30-minute post-mortem tomorrow to review root cause and follow-ups (config + perf work)?

— Neha
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

> > Quick update from infra: we've correlated the customer's timestamps...

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Khan <elena.khan@finovia.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained response-time outliers from Finovia - request for investigation

Elena — thanks again for raising this and for the patience. Quick summary for your execs:

What happened:
- Short-lived request bursts caused an edge-pool saturation where our conservative per-tenant concurrency cap + backpressure heuristics produced long queue waits for a small fraction of requests, producing p99 spike and a bump in 5xx.

What we did (mitigation):
- Temporarily doubled per-tenant concurrency cap on the affected pool and disabled the delay heuristic for the variant. p99 reduced from ~9s to ~1s; 5xx dropped to baseline.
- Activated an auto-fallback guardrail and increased tracing sampling; no cross-tenant impact observed during the window.

Next steps (follow-up):
1) Performance patch: runtime team to tune KV cache windowing and reduce miss penalty (ETA: 72 hours).
2) Config change: consider adjusting default per-tenant concurrency floor for bursty customers (product discussion).
3) Post-mortem: 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through logs and agree SLO updates and customer-level mitigations.

I'll be on the post-mortem. If your execs want a short one-page incident summary, we can provide it after the post-mortem.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-brief-draft-link (will follow), hubspot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/ticket/FIN-2026-07-19
